root_cause: One-shot generation with no execution feedback: empty-result queries caused by literal-value mismatch (case/trailing space), wrong filter column, and NULL-unsafe NOT IN are returned unchecked
what: Add a draft->execute->repair loop (2 policy calls max): the harness runs the first query and, when it errors or returns zero rows, probes actual stored values (LIKE/LOWER sample of the literals used) and re-prompts with the error/empty result plus those samples and targeted guidance (match substrings case-insensitively, pick the right text column, avoid NOT IN over nullable columns). Also tighten the system prompt on Spider conventions ('details'/unspecified attributes -> all columns of the main table; exact string-literal semantics).
decision: Only admissible candidate and it improves evolve score (83.33 -> 86.67) with zero broken tasks; the draft->execute->evidence-backed repair loop is a general text-to-SQL mechanism rather than task-specific patching, so the ~413 extra tokens/task are justified despite only 1 of 4 predicted fixes landing.

root_cause: Repair turn is starved of evidence: it only probes literals already in the draft against arbitrary columns, so clean-but-empty queries caused by filtering on the wrong column (or on non-existent columns) get no information about where the value actually lives
what: Rewrite the evidence gatherer in solve.py: probe keywords taken from the question/hint as well as the SQL literals against every text column of every table (exact/case-insensitive first, then substring), list distinct values of short low-cardinality text columns, and report SQLite errors from probes (which enumerate real column names, exposing hallucinated filter/join columns); feed this plus a wrong-column checklist into the existing single repair call.

root_cause: Repair turn is triggered only by errors/zero rows and its guidance is a fixed literal-matching checklist, so (a) cleanly-executing but semantically wrong drafts are never re-examined and (b) empty-result repairs get no column-level evidence about WHERE the mentioned value actually lives
what: Rework solve.py's second call: probe every text column for question-quoted phrases AND distinctive question words (reporting exact hits with counts vs. substring-only hits), attach an FK join map plus small distinct-value samples of short low-cardinality text columns referenced by the draft, show the draft's first result rows, and trigger the repair on execution error, zero rows, or a static alias-shadowing check on correlated subqueries; replace the fixed checklist with neutral, evidence-driven diagnostic instructions. Also soften the projection rule in system_prompt.md from a blanket 'select all columns' to 'unspecified attributes -> that entity's own table columns', since a bare 'Which X ...' identification question does not ask for unspecified attributes.
